title: Molecular Identification of Phytopathogenic Fungi
author: Unknown
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.shteb6n
materials: Amplified the internal transcribed spacer region, including the 5.8S rDNA, using universal primers ITS1 (5’- TCCGTAGGTGAACCTGCGG-3’) and ITS4 (5’- TCCTCCGCTTATTGATATGC-3’) Carried out PCR reaction in 25 µL, consisting of 25 ng of DNA, 1× PCR buffer (Invitrogen), 0.20 mM of each dNTP (Invitrogen), 1.5 mM MgCl 2 , 1 µM of each primer and 1U Taq polymerase (Invitrogen). Perform DNA amplification in a thermal cycler as GeneAmp 9700 DNA Thermal Cycler (Perkin-Elmer) Amplification program consisted of an initial denaturing step at 95° for 1 min, followed by 30 cycles of 1 min at 94°C, 1 min at 58°C and 1 min at 72°C, and a final extension step of 7 min at 72°C. PCR product can be visualized by electrophoresis in 1.5% (w/v) agarose gels and ethidium bromide staining. The band size obtained will be between 500 and 800 base pairs, depending on the filamentous fungus species studied. The quantity and quality of DNA obtained must be determined. DNA quantified spectrophotometrically and DNA quality by calculating the A260/A280 ratio.

steps.title: Prepare Fungal Mycelia
steps.instruction: Cultivate and collect mycelia from the target fungus.

substeps.instruction: Obtain 10 agar culture discs (1 x 1 cm) from a 7-day-old colony grown on PDA or another culture medium.
Transfer discs into 250-ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 50 ml of nutrient broth (NB) medium.
Incubate at 28°C on an orbital shaker (100 rpm) for three or four days.
Collect mycelia by filtration.
Either freeze mycelia at -80°C until use, or freeze at -80°C for 2 hours, lyophilize, and store (optional).

steps.title: Lyse Fungal Cells
steps.instruction: Mechanically and chemically disrupt the fungal mycelia to release DNA.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend fungal mycelia in 1000 µL of sterile distilled water and add two 5-mm sterile porcelain beads.
Vortex at full speed for 3–5 min.
Freeze at –80°C for 10 min.
Defrost in a water bath at 65°C for 3 min and vortex at full speed again for 3 min.
Transfer 300 µL of cell suspension to a new 2-mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 800 µL of lysing buffer.
Incubate at 65°C for 30 min, with occasional inversion.
Cool the mixture to room temperature (RT).

steps.title: Extract and Purify DNA
steps.instruction: Isolate the DNA from the lysate using chloroform and isopropanol precipitation.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of chloroform and invert gently for 10 min.
Centrifuge for 10 min at 15,682g at RT.
Transfer the top aqueous layer to a new 2-mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 700 µL of chilled isopropanol and mix by very gentle inversion.
Incubate for 10 min at –80°C.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 15,682g at RT and discard the supernatant.
Wash the pellet with 500 µL of 70% ethanol.
Dry under vacuum centrifugation (optional).
Resuspend the dry pellet in 50 µL of TE buffer.

steps.title: Sequence and Analyze DNA
steps.instruction: Purify PCR products and perform sequence alignment.

substeps.instruction: Purify and sequence the obtained PCR products.
Align and edit fungal sequences using the Bio Edit Sequence Alignment program.
